name: Hereditary Xerocytosis with PIEZO1 Mutation

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic PIEZO1 mutation by molecular genetic testing
Evidence of erythrocyte dehydration demonstrated by decreased osmotic fragility and altered red cell indices
Presence of chronic hemolytic anemia with reticulocytosis and elevated indirect bilirubin
Exclusion of other causes of hemolytic anemia such as hereditary spherocytosis or autoimmune hemolytic anemia
Peripheral blood smear showing stomatocytes and dehydrated erythrocytes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic PIEZO1 mutation plus clinical and laboratory evidence of erythrocyte dehydration and hemolytic anemia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires molecular confirmation due to phenotypic overlap with other hemolytic anemias.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic cellular dehydration causing altered red cell morphology

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of stomatocytes on peripheral blood smear

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to chronic hemolysis or transfusions

rare.notes: Reported in some cases, possibly related to splenectomy

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear with stomatocytes and dehydrated erythrocytes
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in PIEZO1 gene confirmed by molecular testing
other: Absence of autoantibodies against red blood cells
Normal or mildly elevated serum ferritin unless transfused

distinguishingFeatures: Spherocytes on blood smear instead of stomatocytes
Mutations in ankyrin, spectrin or band 3 genes
Distinct electrophysiological red cell membrane abnormalities

redFlags: Signs of iron overload despite no transfusions
references: Andolfo I, Russo R, Gambale A, et al. Hereditary xerocytosis: clinical and molecular heterogeneity. Blood. 2013;121(22):3925-3935.
Albuisson J, Murthy SE, Bandell M, et al. Dehydrated hereditary stomatocytosis linked to gain-of-function mutations in mechanically activated PIEZO1 ion channels. Nat Commun. 2013;4:1884.
